title: Sorted Array Deduplication
statement:
Compact a sorted array so each value appears once at the front.

Contract
- `numbers` is non-null and sorted in nondecreasing order. It may be empty.
- Rewrite the beginning of `numbers` so positions `0` through `returnedCount - 1` contain the distinct values in ascending order.
- Return the number of distinct values. Values after that prefix may be left unchanged.
- Use constant extra space.

Examples
- `deduplicate(new int[]{1, 1, 2})` returns `2` and leaves prefix `[1, 2]`.
- `deduplicate(new int[]{-3, -3, -1, 0, 0, 5})` returns `4` with prefix `[-3, -1, 0, 5]`.
- `deduplicate(new int[]{})` returns `0`.
hints: Keep one write pointer for the next unique slot.
A value is new when it differs from the last value written to the prefix.
Scan once from left to right and overwrite only the prefix. Intended complexity: O(n) time and O(1) extra space.
inputSyntax: Input: a sorted integer array, for example: [1, 1, 2]
